cohort: The study included 619 pregnant women who delivered at a hospital in Ghana between January 1, 2021, and December 31, 2021.
finding: The overall prevalence of preeclampsia was 10.5%, with the highest gestational age-specific prevalence at 39-40 weeks, and independent risk factors included maternal age 30-39 years, gestational age < 37 weeks, and previous caesarean section, with small head circumference identified as an associated complication.
mod_finding: Caesarean section was identified as an independent predictor of preeclampsia (aOR = 2.83).
cross-section timing: Data was collected retrospectively from birth registers for deliveries occurring between January 1, 2021, and December 31, 2021.
gest_age: Gestational age categories included <37 weeks, 37-38 weeks, 39-40 weeks, 41 weeks, and >=42 weeks.
